newsitem.title: UK: US FUNDS BUYING STOCKS, EXPECT INFLATION - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: US FUNDS BUYING STOCKS, EXPECT INFLATION - SURVEY.

text.p: U.S. fund managers are buying domestic equities but expect further economic strength to bring inflation, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

The survey, which covered 42 institutions with 1.6 trillion under management, showed that buyers of U.S. equities outnumbered sellers in August by five percent, the first positive since December 1995.
But 45 percent of U.S. fund managers expect inflation to rise over the coming year, up from 28 percent last month. And 38 percent see the U.S. economy further strengthening in the same period.
Fund managers are also buyers of domestic bonds, with buyers outnumbering sellers by 14 percent in August, up from 3 percent last month.
"This renewed buying interest may have been sparked off by Alan Greenspan's comments in the July Humphrey Hawkins testimony," Merrill Lynch said.
U.S. fund managers are neutral on UK equities but positive on European shares, with buyers outnumbering sellers by five percent.
There is continued strong interest in Japanese and Latin American equities, with buyers outnumbering sellers for both assets by more than 20 percent.
But sentiment about Pacific basin countries, not including Japan, has turned steeply negative. On a three-month view, bears on the region outnumber bulls by 33 percent.
The survey was carried out for Merrill by Gallup between August 1 and 6.
